days.subject: Your SitComfort has arrived. Your 7-Day Reset starts tomorrow
days.preview: One short step and a short video each morning. Here's your week.
days.title: Welcome to Your 7-Day Reset
days.subtitle: What to Expect This Week
days.intro: Your order has been delivered. It comes with our free 7-Day Reset: one short step and a short video each morning for a week, to help you sit comfortably for longer.
days.tip: For today, just unpack and use your cushion as normal. Tomorrow we start from the ground up.
days.reply_prompt: Before we start: what brought you to SitComfort? Back pain, long workdays, lots of driving? Hit reply and tell us, so we can help with your situation.
days.note: One small favour: if this email landed in your Promotions tab, drag it into Primary so you don't miss tomorrow's Day 1.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow morning: Day 1, Your Sitting Foundation.

days.subject: Day 1 of 7: let's fix how you sit
days.preview: Four small alignment checks that make everything else work.
days.title: Your Sitting Foundation
days.intro: Today is the base everything else builds on: how you actually sit. Most of us sit badly for 8+ hours a day without noticing. These four checks take 30 seconds.
steps: Not crossed, not tucked under the chair.
Sit on your sit bones, not your tailbone.
Away from your ears, relaxed rather than pulled.
days.tip: Try the four checks now, while you read this. Then once more after lunch.
days.reply_prompt: Quick question: where do you feel it most after a long sit? Lower back, neck, or hips? Just hit reply. We read every message.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: setting up your cushion and lumbar support so good posture takes less effort.
days.subtitle: Foot, Hip & Shoulder Alignment

days.subject: Day 2 of 7: set up your support in 3 minutes
days.preview: Where your cushion and lumbar support should actually sit.
days.title: Setting Up Your Support
days.intro: Yesterday you set your alignment. Today we add the support layer, so holding that position stops feeling like work.
steps: Place the seat cushion at the back
Push it right into the back of the seat, not floating forward. Your hips tilt slightly forward and your spine stacks naturally.
Set the lumbar support at belt height
It should meet the natural curve of your lower back.
Lean back and let it work
The support holds your spine so your muscles can relax.
days.tip: If it feels odd for the first hour, that's normal. Your body is getting used to sitting upright again.
days.reply_prompt: Not sure you've got the position right? Reply with a photo of your chair setup and we'll check it for you.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: your screen, desk and keyboard.
days.subtitle: Cushion + Lumbar Positioning

days.subject: Day 3 of 7: your screen, desk and keyboard
days.preview: Small workspace tweaks that stop you leaning forward.
days.title: Screen, Desk & Keyboard Setup
days.intro: Your workspace either supports your posture or pulls you out of it. Today's tweaks take five minutes and stop the forward lean that undoes your setup.
steps: The top of the screen at, or just below, eye level.
Hands rest on the keyboard with elbows bent at about a right angle.
Wrists neutral, mouse right next to the keyboard.
days.tip: On a laptop? A stack of books under it plus a cheap external keyboard makes a big difference.
days.reply_prompt: Working from a laptop, a sofa or a kitchen table? Reply and tell us. We'll send a tip for your setup.
days.subtitle: Monitor Height, Depth & Peripherals

days.subject: Day 4 of 7: breaking the slouch habit
days.preview: The 20-second reset that keeps you upright all day.
days.title: Breaking the Slouch Habit
days.intro: Your setup is done. Now for the part that makes it last: small, regular resets so slouching never gets the chance to settle in.
steps: Every 20 minutes, take 20 seconds to re-check your posture.
Sit tall, roll your shoulders back and down, tuck your chin slightly.
Get up, stretch, walk, grab water. Movement is medicine.
days.tip: Set a silent 20-minute repeating timer on your phone or watch for the next two days. After that it starts to become automatic.
days.reply_prompt: Halfway there. On a scale of 1 to 10, how does sitting feel compared with Day 1? Reply with a number.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: quick desk stretches to release tension.
days.subtitle: The 20/20 Rule & Standing Every 60–90 Min

days.subject: Day 5 of 7: quick desk stretches that release tension
days.preview: Chest opener, chin tucks, hip flexor stretch and thoracic rotation, right at your desk.
days.title: Move Better, Feel Better
days.intro: Even good posture gets stiff if you hold it all day. Today's video walks you through four quick stretches you can do right at your desk, no gym gear needed.
steps: Opens up the front of your shoulders after hours hunched over a keyboard.
Gently draw your chin straight back, as if making a double chin. Great for neck tension from screen time.
Releases the front of your hips, which tighten up when you sit for long periods.
One hand behind your head, sit tall and rotate through your upper back.
days.tip: Pair the routine with something you already do, like your mid-morning coffee, so it sticks.
days.reply_prompt: Which stretch did you feel the most? Reply and let us know.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: putting it all together into one daily routine.
days.subtitle: Quick Desk Stretches

days.subject: Day 6 of 7: reset, work, move (your daily routine)
days.preview: How the whole week fits into one simple workday routine.
days.title: Reset. Work. Move.
days.intro: You've learned the pieces. Today's video shows how they fit together into one simple routine for your workday, so it happens without thinking about it.
steps: Start each work block with your Day 1 checks, cushion and lumbar support in place.
Screen at eye level, elbows at 90°. Use the 20/20 rule to catch slouching early.
Stand every 60–90 minutes and run through your 4 desk stretches from Day 5.
days.tip: Write "Reset. Work. Move." on a sticky note and put it on your screen for the next week.
days.reply_prompt: Which part of the routine is hardest to stick to? Reply and tell us. We might have a tip.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: the last day, and what changed in 7 days.
days.subtitle: Your Full Daily Routine

days.subject: Day 7 of 7: look how far you've come
days.preview: Compare how you sat 7 days ago, and how to keep it going.
days.title: 7 Days, One Simple System
days.intro: Think back to how you sat 7 days ago. In today's video we compare before and after, and show the simple system that made the difference.
steps: The 20/20 check is the single most useful habit from this week.
Walk, stretch or do light strength work most days.
Discomfort is a signal, not a failure. Adjust and reset.
Let your support do the work
Your cushion and lumbar support keep you aligned every day.
days.tip: Bookmark the 7-Day Reset page. Run through it again any time things start to slip.
days.reply_prompt: We'd love to hear your before and after. Reply with one thing that changed for you this week. It genuinely makes our day.
